units.prompt_text:
Identity: the person in @image1, exactly; same face and costume as the reference for the whole clip.
Setting: Pedestrian crossing at a busy junction, grey city street, kerb on the near side of the road, signal pole behind her. Passers-by, if any, are soft blurred shapes who never react.
Camera: wide, slightly low angle, full body head to trainers; slow handheld push-in begins, gentle bob, camera noticing her before she notices it. No cuts.
Physics: each held object stays in a named hand or rests on a surface; nothing floats or vanishes; mouth closed on anything in it; feet grounded except described steps; everything else holds still.
0-3s: Both arms raised, hands open as a conductor, slam down on THREE and rise on TWO; red standing figure glows on the signal behind her; whistle hangs on its cord; feet planted. Captain Tempo says: "THREE!". Captain Tempo says: "TWO!".
3-6s: Right hand lifts the whistle to sealed lips and blows once, then drops it on its cord and shouts ONE; left arm hangs; feet planted; signal still. Captain Tempo says: "ONE!".
6-9s: Both fists thrust skyward after two trainer stomps and a hip swing; whistle swings on its cord; signal flips on its own timer; camera and crowd hold steady. Captain Tempo says: "AND!".
9-12s: Both fists held up in the frozen pose, whistle hanging on its cord, grin steady; a commuter walks past; feet planted; signal and camera hold still.
Sound: only the quoted lines are spoken; real junction traffic, footsteps and crowd murmur, idling engines; no music.
No readable text, logos or signage. Natural skin, natural hands, no blur on the face.
units.prompt_text_full:
TOP PRIORITY (read first):
1. Face and identity match @image1 100% for the entire take; identity reference ONLY, never its lighting.
2. Speak ONLY the quoted lines, in English, lips still when no line is spoken.
3. Props exist from frame one and never appear, disappear or change design: referee whistle on red cord, small handheld metronome clipped to waistband, white sweatband, pedestrian signal head showing red standing figure then green walking figure (pictograms only, no text), blurred generic pedestrians (extras).
4. Never staged, never stiff, never puppet-like; the comedy is in disproportion, not mugging.
5. No readable brand text, logos or signage anywhere in frame.
=== REFERENCE KEY === @image1 character reference; @image2 location still (scene reference only).
CHARACTER: Lean weathered face, deep laugh lines, bright wide-set grey eyes, short silver hair cropped close at the sides and spiky on top, very mobile eyebrows, a wide gap-toothed grin. Costume: Glossy teal and gold tracksuit zipped to the chin, white sweatband, a referee whistle on a red cord, chunky white trainers, a small handheld metronome clipped to the waistband; glossy teal tracksuit trousers with a gold side stripe. Same outfit throughout the episode.. Register: Big, physical, loud, breathless, joyful; arms conduct, legs bounce, the whistle blows; the comedy is total commitment to a pointless job plus the world's indifference.
CRITICAL - RELIGHT: discard the reference's lighting; relight to the scene as described per shot, with true contact shadows; must look physically present, never a cut-out.
--- S1 (0.0-3.0s) ---
Location: Pedestrian crossing at a busy junction, grey city street, kerb on the near side of the road, signal pole behind her. Environment: Busy junction, grey tarmac and kerb, a stream of generic pedestrians as soft blurred shapes with no faces readable, distant traffic out of focus, no readable signs, logos or text.
Action: Wide, slightly low across the road: Captain Tempo stands at the kerb, both arms raised, hands open, red standing figure glowing on the signal behind her. Her arms drop on THREE and rise again on TWO, mouth open to shout, whistle hanging on its cord and metronome clipped to the waistband; the handheld camera begins its slow push-in. Feet, signal pole and kerb stay still.
Performance: Stern conductor's stare at the crowd, jaw set, open-mouthed shouts of THREE and TWO, whistle hanging on its cord. Micro-expression: Eyebrows shoot up on the downbeat, then lock into a stern frown.
Camera: wide, slightly low angle, full body head to trainers; lens feel phone main camera feel, wide (about 24mm equivalent); movement slow handheld push-in begins, gentle bob, camera noticing her before she notices it; rig handheld phone, operator walking slowly forward from across the road
Lighting: Overcast daylight key from high camera-left, soft; fill from the open grey sky; warm gold bounce off her tracksuit stripe onto her jaw and forearms and teal bounce onto the pavement beside her; soft contact shadows under her trainers and each pedestrian. Light stays constant, no clouds breaking.
Audio: ambience real junction traffic, footsteps and crowd murmur, idling engines; foley: metronome tick on the waistband, tracksuit fabric swish as arms drop, trainer scuff on kerb, whistle cord swinging against her chest; no music
Dialogue (Captain Tempo, on-camera): "THREE!" - hoarse booming shout on the downbeat, rhythmic
Dialogue (Captain Tempo, on-camera): "TWO!" - louder, whistle hanging on its cord
--- S2 (3.0-6.0s) ---
Location: Pedestrian crossing at a busy junction, grey city street, kerb on the near side of the road, signal pole behind her. Environment: Busy junction, grey tarmac and kerb, a stream of generic pedestrians as soft blurred shapes with no faces readable, distant traffic out of focus, no readable signs, logos or text.
Action: Push-in continues. Her right hand lifts the whistle by the cord to her sealed lips and blows one blast, no speech, no grin, left arm hanging at her side. She lets go and the whistle drops to hang on its cord at her chest, then she shouts ONE, knees bending. Feet, signal pole and kerb stay still.
Performance: Eyes fixed on the crowd; lips sealed on the whistle for the blast, then mouth open for ONE with the whistle hanging. Micro-expression: Cheeks puff on the sealed-lip blast, then a quick sideways glance at the signal.
Camera: wide, low angle, tightening to knees-up as the push-in closes; lens feel phone main camera feel, wide (about 24mm equivalent); movement continuing slow low-angle handheld push-in, bob grows slightly with her bounce; rig handheld phone, operator walking slowly forward from across the road
Lighting: Overcast daylight key from high camera-left, soft; fill from the open grey sky; warm gold bounce off her tracksuit stripe onto her jaw and forearms and teal bounce onto the pavement beside her; soft contact shadows under her trainers and each pedestrian. Light stays constant, no clouds breaking.
Audio: ambience real junction traffic, footsteps and crowd murmur, idling engines; foley: sharp referee whistle blast, whistle cord slapping her chest, metronome rattling with her bounce, tracksuit swish; no music
Dialogue (Captain Tempo, on-camera): "ONE!" - roaring, breathless, almost a bark, whistle hanging on its cord
--- S3 (6.0-9.0s) ---
Location: Pedestrian crossing at a busy junction, grey city street, kerb on the near side of the road, signal pole behind her. Environment: Busy junction, grey tarmac and kerb, a stream of generic pedestrians as soft blurred shapes with no faces readable, distant traffic out of focus, no readable signs, logos or text.
Action: On AND she shouts, mouth open, and the signal behind her flips from red standing figure to green walking figure on its own timer. Her white trainers stomp twice, her hips swing and both empty fists thrust to the sky; the whistle swings on its cord. The blurred crowd begins crossing without looking at her. Signal pole and kerb stay still.
Performance: Holds the instant of the flip with certainty, then grins wide through the Tempo Stomp, whistle hanging on its cord. Micro-expression: Gap-toothed grin explodes wide, eyebrows lifting skyward with the fists.
Camera: wide, low angle, full body, towering silhouette against grey sky; lens feel phone main camera feel, wide (about 24mm equivalent); movement low-angle handheld push-in slows to a settle as she peaks, one small wobble on the stomp impact; rig handheld phone, operator walking slowly forward from across the road
Lighting: Overcast daylight key from high camera-left, soft; fill from the open grey sky; warm gold bounce off her tracksuit stripe onto her jaw and forearms and teal bounce onto the pavement beside her; soft contact shadows under her trainers and each pedestrian. Light stays constant, no clouds breaking.
Audio: ambience real junction traffic, footsteps and crowd murmur, idling engines; foley: two heavy trainer stomps, tracksuit swish on hip swing, whistle cord swinging, metronome clack, green-signal beep tone, generic and unlabelled; no music
Dialogue (Captain Tempo, on-camera): "AND!" - one explosive shout, held, joyful
--- S4 (9.0-12.0s) ---
Location: Pedestrian crossing at a busy junction, grey city street, kerb on the near side of the road, signal pole behind her. Environment: Busy junction, grey tarmac and kerb, a stream of generic pedestrians as soft blurred shapes with no faces readable, distant traffic out of focus, no readable signs, logos or text.
Action: Fists still in the air, Captain Tempo holds her frozen victory pose, beaming, whistle hanging on its cord at her chest. A single blurred commuter in a dark coat walks calmly through the frame between her raised fists and the camera, hair-width from her, never looking over. Her feet and the camera hold still, then the camera rests, no cut.
Performance: Proud grin held, eyes locked on camera, pose unbroken as the commuter passes. Micro-expression: Proud grin holds, one eyebrow twitches up as the commuter passes.
Camera: wide settling to medium-wide, low angle, full figure held; lens feel phone main camera feel, wide (about 24mm equivalent); movement camera settles into a final held framing with a small handheld breathe, no cut; rig handheld phone, operator walking slowly forward from across the road
Lighting: Overcast daylight key from high camera-left, soft; fill from the open grey sky; warm gold bounce off her tracksuit stripe onto her jaw and forearms and teal bounce onto the pavement beside her; soft contact shadows under her trainers and each pedestrian. Light stays constant, no clouds breaking.
Audio: ambience real junction traffic, footsteps and crowd murmur, idling engines; foley: commuter footsteps passing, fabric brush of the passing coat, distant traffic, one last metronome tick; no music
ON-SCREEN TEXT: none (added in post).
